correctness.rationale: The open-neighborhood cover U union V has two explicitly collapsible sphere pieces. Its exact intersection is the connected crown graph of cycle rank n^2-3n+1. The inclusions from the one-dimensional graph into simply connected sphere pieces are nullhomotopic for n>=4; the cofibration homotopy pushout yields the full integral wedge. For n>=5 Mayer–Vietoris gives the zero-row/column-sum integral lattice and sign-twisted two-point top representation; chain-level transposition and signed Lefschetz checks verify the character formulas. Direct full face checks n=4..8 and 1680 exact signed elementwise Lefschetz checks at n=5,6 passed, while the general proof is independent of sample size.

originality.rationale: The literature and published-record comparisons directly address the exact open neighborhood object, its complement-of-crown alias, its 2-by-n rook-graph identification and the full symmetric action. The closest all-parameter open rook theorem assumes both dimensions >=3; a related clique-cycle result assumes cycles >=5 and contains a circle absent here; a closed-neighborhood result is mathematically distinct. The character polynomial alone overlaps related Kneser work, but this theorem determines the separate full homotopy and layer-swap representation rather than claiming that polynomial in isolation.

value.rationale: This completes the natural omitted two-row boundary of rook-graph open-neighborhood topology for every n>=4, where a quadratic family of 2-spheres coexists with two spheres of dimension n-2. Unlike a finite case or a Betti-only calculation it resolves the homotopy attaching maps and the full integral S_n by C2 module, including the nontrivial layer-swap transposition and an acyclic rational orbit space. The natural graph family and representation make the result useful as an exact boundary example for neighborhood complexes and equivariant homotopy.
